children: London's Heathrow Airport said passenger numbers fell slightly in October, as the Middle East conflict continues to weigh on traffic.
The airport--jointly owned by the Qatar Investment Authority, China Investment Corp. and others--said Wednesday that passenger numbers dropped 1.0% in October to 7.3 million.
Middle East traffic slumped 21% from a year ago to 563,000 passengers as the conflict in the region continued. EU traffic edged down 0.3% while non-EU Europe traffic grew 5.2%.
North America traffic increased 1.1% and Latin America traffic rose 1.6%. Traffic for the Asia-Pacific region climbed 7.5%, but Africa travel was 1.1% lower. Domestic traffic for the U.K. fell 6.0%.
Heathrow said airlines remain keen to expand their presence at the airport.
